advances: Exact ownership and fixed-budget comparison in one above-target family with baseline normalized depth 4/9.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Apply the strict five-triangle all-normal depth result to this exact radius array and area measure. It gives the three canonical normals $u_1=(1,0),u_2=(0,1),u_3=(-1,-1)$, the proper cyclic charts, the exact middle depth $D_0$, and slack groups at the two inner centroids covering their respective two bases. These slack groups can be held fixed and keep their masses below $Q$ nearby, since their baseline mass bounds are strictly below $Q$.

A middle cap in chart $i$ has margin $(u_i+\theta_i u_{i+1})\cdot x+\alpha_i z$. With equal positive weights continuous balance requires $\theta_1=\theta_2=\theta_3$, since $u_1+u_2+u_3=0$ is the only relation up to scaling. For sufficiently small chart neighborhoods the three continuous normals span the plane and the space of relations is one-dimensional. With any balanced positive weights $w_i$, the middle caps cover the whole plane at a base $z$ precisely when $z\sum_i w_i\alpha_i\ge0$. If the sum is nonnegative, some margin is nonnegative at every point. If it is negative, the $3$-by-$2$ matrix of continuous normals has column image equal to the plane orthogonal to $(w_1,w_2,w_3)$. There is then an $x$ for which all three margins equal the negative number $z\sum_i w_i\alpha_i/\sum_i w_i$. The equal-weight right assignment consequently needs $\sum_i\alpha_i\le0$ and the left needs $\sum_i\alpha_i\ge0$.

In a common proper chamber the all-normal formula, written by completing the square, is
$$
\Phi(\alpha,\theta)=
\frac{(2-\theta)^2}{2(1-\theta)}(R+Eb^2)
+\frac5{1-\theta}[\alpha+(2-\theta)a]^2 .
$$
If the unconstrained minimizer $\theta=0,\alpha=-2a$ has the required sign, use it for all three caps and attain $D_0$. If $a<0$ in the right assignment, at least one $\alpha_i\le0$. Its free optimum at fixed $\theta_i$ is $-(2-\theta_i)a>0$, so its cap mass is bounded below by the value at $\alpha_i=0$. This latter value is $(2-\theta_i)^2(R+10a^2+Eb^2)/[2(1-\theta_i)]$, at least $D_0+20a^2$ with equality at $\theta_i=0$. Taking all three tilts and all three angular changes zero attains this lower bound. For the left assignment and $a>0$, the same square is minimized on $\alpha_i\ge0$ at zero, giving the stated left formula. In both cases all active middle caps have equal masses at the exhibited optimum. The wrong-side lower bound uses only positivity of the weights and the sign condition. Equal-weight optima are admissible in the class allowing smoothly varying positive weights, so that class has the same quadratic terms. The chosen assignment attains $D_0$ and no through-middle-centroid cap can have smaller mass by the all-normal depth formula.

A frozen canonical cap has mass $2(R+10a^2+Eb^2)$, giving second derivative $40A^2+4EB^2=40A^2+(456/25)B^2$. For a right optimum the second derivative per cap is $4EB^2+40(A_-)^2$, and for a left optimum it is $4EB^2+40(A_+)^2$. Total area has second derivative $90A^2+9EB^2$ in either case. Subtracting $3/4$ times the second derivative of the three-cap sum gives the stated right and left values, and the unconstrained choice after optimizing ownership gives $90A^2$. These are right derivatives at zero along the indicated velocities, which retains the sidedness of the fixed assignments.

The invertible map $(z,x)\mapsto(z,kx)$ preserves the integer bases and sends each cap of margin $u\cdot x+\alpha(z-j)$ to one of margin $u\cdot x+k\alpha(z-j)$ at the image coordinates. The map multiplies each fiber area and all halfspace masses by $k^2$, preserves the cover and its slack, and therefore multiplies the true global raw depth by $k^2$. With the given choice, $k^2D_0=Q$. Multiplying the total area $V(R+10a^2+Eb^2)$ by $k^2$ gives the displayed formula since $10V=45$. Its increment is positive exactly when $a\ne0$, and the common raw depth then forces strict normalized descent.
statement:
Use the strict five-triangle family with $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)\}$, bases $P=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and radii $r_j+aj+be_j$, where $r=(4/5,19/20,1,19/20,4/5)$ and $e=(1,0,-8/5,0,1)$. Write $R=817/200$, $E=114/25$, $Q=2R$, $D_0=Q+2Eb^2$, and $a_\pm=\max\{\pm a,0\}$. In the proper cyclic middle-cap chamber with equal positive cover weights, assigning the middle group to cover bases $\{-2,-1,0\}$ and the right slack group to cover $\{1,2\}$ gives smallest largest middle-cap mass $D_0+20a_-^2$. The assignment with middle bases $\{0,1,2\}$ and left slack bases $\{-2,-1\}$ gives $D_0+20a_+^2$. Choosing the better assignment attains $D_0$ and is optimal even among unrestricted through-middle-centroid cap choices.

Along $(a,b)=t(A,B)$ for $t\ge0$, the frozen middle-cap second derivative is $40A^2+(456/25)B^2$. With the stress $3/4$ on each middle cap, the second derivatives of total mass minus the stressed sum of optimized middle-cap masses are $90(A_+)^2$ for the right assignment, $90(A_-)^2$ for the left, and $90A^2$ after assignment optimization. The same quadratic terms hold with smoothly varying positive balance weights equal at the baseline.

Finally, the common continuous homothety of scale $k$ with $k^2=R/(R+Eb^2)$ fixes the actual global raw depth at $Q$ and gives total mixed area
$$
M(0,0)+\frac{45Ra^2}{R+Eb^2}.
$$
Thus it gives strict fixed-budget volume gain and strict decrease of normalized maximum depth exactly when $a\ne0$. The full $b$ axis is neutral after this normalization.
title: Two ownership choices and an exact fixed-budget neutral axis
